title: Tokenization — Segmentation Creates a Modeling Tradeoff
key_insight: A larger vocabulary shortens sequences but expands the embedding and output tables. A smaller vocabulary saves table parameters but lengthens attention work.
body:
## Segmentation Creates a Modeling Tradeoff

A rare technical term is split into many fragments. The model can represent it, but must rebuild its meaning across more positions.

A larger vocabulary shortens sequences but expands the embedding and output tables. A smaller vocabulary saves table parameters but lengthens attention work.

Byte-level fallbacks guarantee coverage of unusual text. Evaluate compression, unknown handling, and fairness across languages rather than choosing vocabulary size from English alone.
common_mistakes: A tokenizer directly verifies every factual answer.
Every token is always one complete English word.
Token numbers have the same meaning across all models.
mini_exercise: Draw “Segmentation Creates a Modeling Tradeoff” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Every language-model input and output passes through a tokenizer, so its choices affect meaning, length, and cost.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Segmentation Creates a Modeling Tradeoff,” explain Tokenization without assuming the listener knows modern AI.
